title: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection - Scratches Detection on Surfscan SP5
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 7nm Node Manufacturing
author: Robert Kim

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP5 system to detect and classify Scratches defects during final inspection inspection at the 7nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Scratches defects that are critical to yield at the 7nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP5 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP5
- Inspection Type: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Scratches
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 7nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP5 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for final inspection monitoring in the 7nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP5
Software Version: v15.7.613
Recipe: UNPATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_7nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (174 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP5 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Unpatterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Scratches defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 7nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 109 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.8% for Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-06-17
Wafers Tested: 47
Total Defects Found: 629
Defect Density: 200.22 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.8%
Capture Rate: 94.1%
Test Duration: 89 minutes
System Uptime: 96.8%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP5 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Scratches at the 7nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Scratches at 7nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
